subject: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:12:00Z
Subject: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call so we have alignment before we kick off the bake-off: 

Pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent latency at scale (spikes during peak traffic) causing timeouts for customer-facing features
- Cost has been unpredictable with current TGI endpoints on GCP; team wants clearer unit economics
- Memory/throughput limits on your vLLM self-hosted setup for longer-context use cases (4k+ tokens)
- Need for a solution that can run in a VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads down the line

Current stack (as stated):
- vLLM on k8s (self-hosted) for mid-tier traffic
- TGI endpoints on GCP for high-throughput features
- Some caching at app layer, no prefix/KV caching in serving layer today

Success criteria for the bake-off (to validate):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency < 300ms for representative 1-2k token prompts at sustained 10 req/s
2) Cost: measured token-level cost improvement vs current TGI baseline (target: >=20% saving with comparable quality)
3) Quality: no regression on your QPS-sampled evals (we'll run your eval set and compare ROUGE/accuracy and human spot checks)
4) Reliability: graceful degradation with fallback to smaller model variants under load (no client-facing failures)

What we (Redwood) will provide for the bake-off:
- A bake-off checklist & test matrix (attached: redwood-bakeoff-checklist.pdf)
- A test harness that can hit endpoints in parallel and collect latency, throughput, token cost, and quality metrics
- A suggested set of model variants (quantized and FP16) and deployment modes (hosted Redwood, Redwood Dedicated, and a reproducible infra config for private evaluation)

What we need from you:
- A sample prompt set and eval queries (link or S3 upload) - you mentioned you could share ~500 prompts; thanks in advance
- Target traffic profile (seq length distribution, concurrency targets) - helps us pick batching/kv-cache configs
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency, logging retention) to include in the Private run

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- You share sample prompts and an initial acceptance criteria doc by Tue 11/10
- Redwood to run an initial lab pass (vLLM vs TGI vs Redwood hosted) 11/15-11/19
- Demo of bake-off results and recommendation week of 11/22

I'll loop in Vivek (SE) to propose the technical test matrix. If this aligns, I can send an official bake-off statement of work and a DocuSign for the limited test credits.

Thanks - looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-checklist.pdf

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-05T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa - this is great and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and items from our side: 

1) Prompts/eval: I've uploaded our sample prompts and golden responses to S3 (s3://acme-test-data/bakeoff/prompts-v1.json). The set is ~475 prompts across short (<=256), medium (~1k), and long (~4k) contexts.

2) Traffic profile: typical steady-state is 8-12 req/s, with peak bursts up to ~30 req/s for short prompts. Long-context workloads are lower volume but latency sensitive.

3) Acceptance criteria: we agree with your latency and cost goals; please add a quality acceptance threshold (e.g., top-line automated metrics + human pass rate threshold) to your test matrix.

4) Procurement: procurement wants an initial SOW for limited test credits and an estimated cost for a 2-week dedicated lab run. I've CC'd procurement; they'll need the SOW and a DocuSign link for approval.

We'll attach the prompts file in our reply.

John
Head of ML Platform | Acme Corporation
john.doe@acme.com

Attachments: acme_test_prompts.json

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T02:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Hi John / Marissa -

Thanks for the prompt upload, John. Based on the prompts and the traffic profile, here's a proposed quick test matrix for the lab pass (we'll capture exact configs in the SOW):

Test matrix (initial lab pass):
- Models/variants: open-source Llama-family via vLLM (FP16), TGI baseline (your current), Redwood hosted open weights (INT8 / FP16), Redwood Dedicated (quantized INT8)
- Sequence lengths: short (<=256), medium (~1k), long (~4k) - use your sample buckets
- Concurrency: steady 10 req/s, burst 30 req/s for short prompts
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, tokens-per-dollar (unit cost), memory usage, tail-kv cache hit rate, model output quality (automated + human sampling)
- Acceptance criteria (suggested): p95 <= 300ms for short/medium, p95 <= 700ms for long; >=20% cost reduction vs TGI baseline for comparable quality; human evaluators find <=5% regression on critical intents

Operational notes:
- We'll run isolated runs for each endpoint to get baseline metrics, then run a mixed workload pass to validate routing and fallback behavior.
- For the private/Dedicated runs we'll need a temporary VPC peering or a short-lived customer tunnel to pull metrics securely.

Proposed dates: Redwood lab run 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-19. We can deliver an initial report by 11/22 and schedule a results walkthrough the same week.

Next asks from Acme:
- Confirm acceptance criteria above (we can iterate)
- Provide temporary test credentials or enable the test S3 read for our harness
- Procurement: SOW + DocuSign for test credits (Marissa will send)

On the DocuSign - Marissa, I have a short SOW template ready; I can attach a pre-filled SOW if you want me to.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed-bakeoff-matrix.csv

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>

Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-06T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Sounds good - we confirm the timeline and the acceptance criteria as listed by Vivek with one minor tweak: please tighten the long-context p95 target to <= 600ms if possible. Procurement will review the SOW today; they'll need a DocuSign link for signature.

I've attached a signed NDA and SLA excerpt from our side (signed-sla.pdf). Once procurement signs, we'll enable the S3 path and expect the lab run to start on 11/15.

Thanks everyone - excited to see the results.

John
Head of ML Platform | Acme Corporation
